newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Foodland Q2 sales down 1.5 pct. [CORRECTED 04:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Foodland Q2 sales down 1.5 pct. [CORRECTED 04:50 GMT]

text.p: Foodland Associated Ltd said on Thursday that its sales for the second quarter ending January 26 fell 1.5 percent to A$977.95 million and that sales for the 26 weeks to January 26 fell 0.9 percent to A$1.855 billion.
Foodland's sales on a like-for-like basis, adjusted for new stores, fell slightly for the quarter to A$963.30 million from A$963.56 million in the same period a year earlier.
First half sales rose 0.3 percent on a like-for-like basis to A$1.804 billion.
Foodland said that wholesale sales at its Western Australian operations rose (company corrects from "fell") by 1.4 percent after adjusting for the loss of a small retail chain as a customer.
It said the launch of its new Dewsons and Rules franchise groups in November had met with pleasing customer response, particularly in the post-Christmas trading period.
Foodland's retail chain posted a like-for-like sales rise of 11.4 percent for the second quarter, on top of a 7.8 percent like-for-like sales increase in the first quarter.
Like-for-like sales at Foodland's Farmers Deka operations in New Zealand fell 1.4 percent in the second quarter because of soft sales of big ticket items before and after the New Zealand election.
"This compares more favourably with the performances announced to date by other New Zealand retailers," Foodland said.
Foodland's Australian Liquor Marketers posted a 14.4 percent increase in sales for the quarter.

Foodland's 58 percent owned unit Progressive Enterprises Ltd reported on Wednesday that second quarter sales fell 2.8 percent to NZ$550.2 million. On a like-for-like basis, Progressive's sales fell 1.8 percent.
Foodland's share price was down five cents at A$6.01 at 12.05 p.m. (0105 GMT).
